title: Inverse-dynamics torque control of the SR2 hand's fingers under HOM
page_title: Inverse-dynamics torque control of the SR2 hand's fingers under HOM
summary: Inverse-dynamics torque control of the SR2 fingers under HOM, against the SCS0009 position servos on the films' layouts: tracking scores went from 0.24 to 0.23 (twist), 0.11 to 0.05 (roll) and 0.38 to 0.44 (press) with a 63 rad/s loop; off-axis angular velocity 34 to 12 deg/s in the twist; joints at the 0.18 N m limit on most physics steps.

title: Contact estimation for the unsensed pusher of the SR2 hand's pin-push under HOM
page_title: Contact estimation for the unsensed pusher of the SR2 hand's pin-push under HOM
summary: The SR2 pin-push with the pusher unsensed: its contact point estimated within 0.22 mm and its force within 0.25 N of 0.45 N; tracking score 0.34 with exact sensing, 0.23 with the boards' noise and 0.27 with the estimate.

title: Fingertip viewer replayed on a UR5 rod roll, with the finite-element and field model of the roll
page_title: Fingertip viewer replayed on a UR5 rod roll, with the finite-element and field model of the roll
summary: Replayed on a 4 N rod roll of v3 ID 5, the fingertip viewer placed contacts a median 0.49 mm from the robot's contact with the UR5-trained GP and 3.06 mm with the physical model alone; an FE and field model of the roll gives the chips' change at correlation 0.90 and 1.71 times its size.

title: The co-design problem of the SR2 hand talk as one nested formula
page_title: The co-design problem of the SR2 hand talk as one nested formula
summary: The talk's co-design problem built up one term per slide (hand, controller, object size, spaces, tasks, metric, simulation, HOM), then zoomed level by level: Yang et al.'s EA (outer), grasp synthesis, HOM and CEM tuning (inner), and a fast, calibrated, observable simulator (evaluator); 32 atomic LaTeX images and diagrams for the slides.

title: HOM landscapes of the SR2 hand on the measured SCS0009 servo and on MuJoCo 4.0
page_title: HOM landscapes of the SR2 hand on the measured SCS0009 servo and on MuJoCo 4.0
summary: The SCS0009's measured 0.55 N m/rad and 0.59 deg dead band reorder the HOM landscapes (tracking-score rho 0.72 to 0.91 against the 0.72 N m/rad model, rerun spread 0.99 to 1.00); the model's best layouts lose 0.14 to 0.29 of their score on the measured servo. On MuJoCo 4.0 the measured servo's landscapes keep rho 0.94 to 0.97 against 3.6.

title: Tracking score of the HOM tasks and films of the SR2 hand across object sizes
page_title: Tracking score of the HOM tasks and films of the SR2 hand across object sizes
summary: A tracking score (share of the commanded rotation followed, times the share of the task on three pads) replaces the HOM task scores, which gave 0.50 to a still sphere on the roll and 1.00 to a whirling twist; re-picked layouts score 0.23 to 0.35 (twist), 0.22 to 0.32 (roll) and 0.61 to 0.71 (press) at four sizes each.

title: Layout search methods for the SR2 hand under HOM control
page_title: Layout search methods for the SR2 hand under HOM control
summary: On the SR2 hand's 625-layout lattice the EA of Yang et al. with 64 individuals was the most reliable of six search methods: on the SCS0009 roll it came within 0.05 of the grid's best by 6,000 rollouts in 66 % of 200 replays, against 23 to 27 % for particle swarms, 24 % for random search and 0 % for the FP paper's RRT. On the six-coordinate Sobol layouts, searched live, the EA and the 16-particle swarm stalled on layouts already run, and RRT and random search found the best ones; first-principles notes on the EA, PSO, CEM, Pareto fronts and t-SNE.

title: Sphere-pad contact and the simulation stack on MuJoCo 4.0
page_title: Sphere-pad contact and the simulation stack on MuJoCo 4.0
summary: MuJoCo 4.0.0 gives the same sphere-pad contact as 3.6.0; MuJoCo Warp 4.0.0 is 17 to 28 % faster and has noslip, which lowers the hand's grasp slip from 170 to 31 µm/s at 7 to 15 times the step cost. The cad_v3 screwdriver rolls by itself (11° and 90° in 1 s) until ccd_tolerance is 1e-10.

title: Static identification of the SR2 hand's SCS0009 servos in free space on the UR5
page_title: Static identification of the SR2 hand's SCS0009 servos in free space on the UR5
summary: The SR2 hand's SCS0009 servos have a 0.59 deg dead band and 0.55 N m/rad at the datasheet's torque scaled to the measured 5.1 V supply (HOM plant 0.72, no friction). The index and middle yaws stick within about 25 mN m of friction and stop 1.5 to 3.1 deg short of 20 to 40 deg steps.

title: Seat, tag block and cameras for HOM experiments with the SR2 hand on the UR5, in simulation
page_title: Seat, tag block and cameras for HOM experiments with the SR2 hand on the UR5, in simulation
summary: In simulation, a flat seat with a 40 mm arm lift keeps the HOM cylinder scores within 0.011 of the study with the stem clear of the fingers; the sphere's stem touches the fingers at three of five layouts. Two side-mounted D435s track the object to 0.20 mm and 0.13 deg RMS with their poses from the arm.

title: Magnetic crosstalk between the fingertip boards on the SR2 hand
page_title: Magnetic crosstalk between the fingertip boards on the SR2 hand
summary: Uncompensated, the fingertip viewer on the SR2 hand would show a 3.6 N contact in 15.9 % of the thumb's 50 ms frames with nothing touching. A GP of each board's change from its finger's three angles leaves 0 to 3 false frames per board out of 14,916 to 21,000 (0 to 3 with the layout left out of its fit), and injected presses read with 11 to 13 % median force error.

title: Block, capsule, ellipsoid and hemisphere fingertips on the v4b finger of the SR2 hand
page_title: Block, capsule, ellipsoid and hemisphere fingertips on the v4b finger of the SR2 hand
summary: On the v4b finger at 2.5 MPa no fingertip shape beats the 11/22 half-ellipsoid that the hand uses. The best other tip is the half-ellipsoid 7.4 × 8.5 × 16/32 mm. Its J3 on fresh placements is 0.259, against 0.195 for the v4b tip. The difference is +0.064, with a 90 % interval from −0.017 to +0.160. The HOM grasps, forces and contact modes were refined for the v4b tip over scene friction 0.4–1.0. On each other stage-3 tip they score lower, by a median 0.02–0.90 per task. A GPU world-step lasts 2.52 µs on the v4b tip. It lasts 2.06–3.23 µs on the capsules, the other ellipsoids and the hemisphere, and 3.98–4.24 µs on the blocks. Of the twelve tips only two fit the v4b DIP link, cassette and cap as built. With pad 05R4’s magnets, the force at the contact point is resolved to 0.032–0.037 N on every tip in which they fit.

title: Model and transforms of the SR2 hand on the UR5 CB3
page_title: Model and transforms of the SR2 hand on the UR5 CB3
summary: The SR2 hand on the UR5 CB3 is modelled in MuJoCo, full and simplified, with the flange-to-palm transform from the CAD: the palm origin lies at (5.05, 2.02, 138.90) mm in tool0 in clocking k = 1, read from the owner's photo (8.3 px port misfit against 48 to 468 px). The travel boxes are centred about 6 mm outside the driver's positions.

title: One finger layout or several for the HOM tasks of the SR2 hand
page_title: One finger layout or several for the HOM tasks of the SR2 hand
summary: On the SCS0009 one SR2 layout reaches at most 0.84 of each HOM task's best (mean 0.75 against 0.82 with one layout per task, seeds 20-24), and three layouts are needed at 0.9. Per-task grasp, force and contact-mode refinement raises both (0.82 against 0.90) and needs two layouts at 0.9.

title: Grasp, force and contact-mode refinement of SR2 hand layouts under HOM control
page_title: Grasp, force and contact-mode refinement of SR2 hand layouts under HOM control
summary: Refining the grasp, HOM's forces and its contact modes per SR2 layout raised the median validated score of the 30 best SCS0009 layouts by 0.05 (roll) to 0.20 (press) over the best of 16 grasps and reordered the layouts (rho 0.56 to 0.75). On the STS3032, picks tuned at friction 1.0 score 0 at friction 0.4 on three tasks; retuning at 0.4 gains 0.18 to 0.53. Picks searched on the lowest score over friction 0.4-1.0 raise it by 0.21 to 0.56 over the 1.0 picks. One set of forces and modes for all layouts gains 0.19 on the press's 30 best layouts (per-layout tuning 0.20) and less than 0.01 on the twist, the roll and the pin-push. One grasp per layout in an evolutionary search's genome changed its incumbents' median by 0.00, -0.07, +0.06 and +0.17 (twist, roll, pin-push and press) against the layout search at 6,000 rollouts. A particle swarm at CEM's rollouts gained 0.24 on the press against CEM's 0.20, and within 0.02 of CEM on the twist and the roll.

title: SR2 hand layouts under HOM control across finger servos, pad moduli and scene friction
page_title: SR2 hand layouts under HOM control across finger servos, pad moduli and scene friction
summary: The finger servo and the scene friction reorder the HOM layouts (Spearman -0.10 to 0.62 between the work plant and the SCS0009, 0.32 to 0.65 between friction 0.4 and 1.0); pad moduli of 1.25-10 MPa barely do (0.77 to 0.98). One layout for three servos loses at most 0.11.

title: Contact models of the four-magnet fingertips fitted to the UR5 presses
page_title: Contact models of the four-magnet fingertips fitted to the UR5 presses
summary: One pad modulus, 2.47 MPa, fits the presses of three four-magnet v3 fingertips under the 5 mm sphere and the 12.5 mm rod (2.22-2.73 MPa per tip); the scenes now run 2.5 MPa with a 0.04 s relaxation time. At 1-2 N the median force ratio is 1.15 and at 8 N 0.49; the FE with one scale follows the load trend. The held tool creeps 163 um/s at 2.5 MPa against 180 at 10 MPa (impratio 10).

title: Implementation of the HOM controller on the SR2 hand with the v4b fingertip
page_title: Implementation of the HOM controller on the SR2 hand with the v4b fingertip
summary: Walkthrough of the HOM controller's code on the SR2 hand with the v4b fingertip: eleven substeps per 10 ms period, each with the twist's and pin-push's numbers. A period takes 1.9 ms on one CPU core; the GPU controller agreed with the CPU on the held outcome for 92 % and 80 % of 60 grasps per task, as often as two of its own seeds agree.

title: Best SR2 hand layouts across object sizes under HOM control
page_title: Best SR2 hand layouts across object sizes under HOM control
summary: Across 19 object sizes the SR2 hand's best layout under HOM control moves with the object: the thumb's mount moves out 0.6 to 1.1 mm per mm of diameter in all four tasks (0.6 to 1.4 on the SCS0009 servos; a slope of 1 is Borràs and Dollar's workspace rule), found by an evolutionary search in 6,000 rollouts per size and confirmed on the CPU plant at 36 of 38 sizes. With a table under the object, no press and no pinch of a cylinder under 16 mm clears it.

title: Probe on the HEX-E pressing fingertips held on indenter plate v2e
page_title: Probe on the HEX-E pressing fingertips held on indenter plate v2e
summary: Probe on the HEX-E (5 and 2 mm spheres, half rod, two flats) pressing tips held pad up on plate v2e's three seats: 452 of 808 pad points reached against 286 for the finger on the robot; tip's end 40/88 (finger 14), flanks 184/492 (finger 75); pushes 35 deg off the normal on 100 % of face and edge points. Seat strip of 10-30: the pads 40 mm over a 35 x 216 mm strip on one 2x4, the plans replayed clean, and it prints with the probe base and the six tools in 9 h 56 min and 189 g.

title: Hand-object mechanism control on the SR2 hand and the fingertip sensing it needs
page_title: Hand-object mechanism control on the SR2 hand and the fingertip sensing it needs
summary: The HOM controller's MuJoCo version on the SR2 hand tracks as well without fingertip contact points as with them. Joint and object calibration errors of 1 deg and 1 mm make its open-loop pinch force wrong by a median 1.05 N; a loop on the magnetic fingertips' measured force (located to 0.25-0.53 mm, force within about 5 %) brings it to 0.31 N, but the same loop dropped the sphere in 48 of 120 twist runs. On UR5 rolls of three calibrated tips the contact filter cut the estimate's scatter from 0.76 to 0.02 mm, and its error stayed at the estimate's own, 0.46 mm at 4 N.

title: Foundational-pose hand design, the project's layout sampling, and a Pareto front for the SR2 hand
page_title: Foundational-pose hand design, the project's layout sampling, and a Pareto front for the SR2 hand
summary: HOM-controller scores of 8,192 SR2 layouts on four tasks and object sizes, v4b fingertip: synthesizing the grasp per layout and task raised the grid's median twist score from 0.23 to 0.47 on fresh seeds and made 24 % of layouts score above 0.5 on all four tasks (1 % with the foundational pose); the best layouts move with object size and sit on peaks a few millimetres wide, where a smooth score model's gradient fails.

title: Contribution of each UR5 calibration motion on the four-magnet fingertips
page_title: Contribution of each UR5 calibration motion on the four-magnet fingertips
summary: On v3 ID 1 and ID 2, each indenter's presses, the tip's end and slides must be in a tip's calibration: an indenter left out is placed 0.57 to 1.80 mm off against 0.25 to 1.05 mm. Presses over 3.5 N add nothing, twists give no torsion estimate; one tip's calibration places the other's presses 1.02 to 1.30 mm off; the tall indenter and the low sphere disagree by 9 to 13 deg at the same contact.

title: Layout of the indenter plate for the UR5 calibration cell
page_title: Layout of the indenter plate for the UR5 calibration cell
summary: The printed indenter plate blocks the side-by-side map (11 of 162 hovers clear) and the tall suite (38 of 168 actions out of the joint windows). A layout with the 5 mm sphere back right, the holder back left, and the 12.5 mm sphere and the rod in front at 95 and 100 mm clears 84 side hovers and 162 tall actions, and fits the P1S plate.

title: Three v1 fingertips at rest overnight on the ESP32-C6 mux
page_title: Three v1 fingertips at rest overnight on the ESP32-C6 mux
summary: Three v1 fingertips at rest for 8.4 h on the ESP32-C6 mux: 163.0 records/s without a gap, noise 1.88/2.89 uT, no contact at the 2 uT floor and 1 frame at 1 uT (0.1 s, 0.9 N). The thermal correction cut the drift to 4-21 uT; the presses of 10-26 left 10 and 20 uT on ID 1 and ID 2.

title: Magnetic crosstalk between neighbouring fingertips and its removal by the fingers' pose
page_title: Magnetic crosstalk between neighbouring fingertips and its removal by the fingers' pose
summary: Magnetic crosstalk between neighbouring fingertips: over two days and 11 layouts of the SR2 hand the contact viewer with no compensation would show a contact in 15.9 % of the thumb's 50 ms frames with nothing touching (median 3.6 N; middle 4.2 %, index 1.3 %). A GP on the finger's own three angles leaves 0-3 of 14,916-21,000 frames per board (0-3 with each layout left out), and injected UR5 presses read with 11-13 % median force error (8-11 % on the zero pose's noise). At the home layout a finger moving alone changed the other boards by at most 5.4 uT (0.19 N), against up to 166 uT (5.8 N) from a tip's own pose. On the UR5 two four-magnet v3 tips touching changed each other's boards by 39-60 uT, against 21.9 uT per newton of face press on v3 ID 1; at a sharpie's width (W 7-11 mm) the change equals a 0.31-0.64 N face press, 0.12-0.23 N after the dipole model with each tip's net moment (7-16 % of one magnet), which explains 97 % of the change at either held board in 137 hovers (25 and 27 % without). In v2 ID 1's field model a five-N52 neighbour equals 3.8 N at W 10 mm; fitting its pose from both boards keeps the press bound at 0.147-0.176 N (0.147 N with the pose known).

title: Shear, friction coefficient and impratio of the printed fingertip against the UR5 slides
page_title: Shear, friction coefficient and impratio of the printed fingertip against the UR5 slides
summary: UR5 slides of the printed fingertip: friction coefficient 0.37 and 0.44 (PLA sphere on 85A, 1 and 2 N, from the magnitude of the shear at slip), give before slip 266 and 181 um/N at 1 and 2 N; under the trainer's solver every impratio from 20 to 100 makes 7-16 of 24 D1-D8 replays diverge after the drop (CPU), the CPU grasp diverges from 50 and the MuJoCo-Warp grasp never (slip 111 to 50 um/s at 10 to 100); the divergence is the flung tool's spin running away under implicitfast; noslip 10 at impratio 10 cuts the replays' creep 180 to 32 um/s (CPU only); a slide-sized skin matches the loops only at impratio 1000; the friction torque is below the HEX-E's resolution.

title: Elasticity, magnet motion and magnetic readout of the printed fingertip
page_title: Elasticity, magnet motion and magnetic readout of the printed fingertip
summary: FE of the printed pad plus a dipole field model give the 15 magnetometer readings for a load anywhere on the surface. With four N52 magnets in a 5.0 mm checkerboard (pad 05R4, chosen 2026-10-28), at 1 N under a 5 mm sphere the face sinks 214 µm, the magnets move 5.3–6.4 µm and the readings change by 27 µT at the face centre (five magnets: 83 µT). Inverted without training it places v3 ID 1's UR5 presses of 1 N and over within 1.4–1.8 mm and their normal force within 19–24 % (medians); under 1 N it fails (8.1 mm). Fitted to the presses of v3 ID 1 to ID 3 and v2 ID 1, it gives each region's signal per newton within 10 % except the face centre, where the four-magnet tips gave 12.6–14.0 µT/N against the model's 16.4–18.4.

title: Calibration of the magnetic fingertip on the UR5 against a six-axis force sensor
page_title: Calibration of the magnetic fingertip on the UR5 against a six-axis force sensor
summary: UR5 + HEX-E calibration of eleven printed magnetic fingertips (43,696 holds, 2026-10-22 to 11-04): a GP from the 15 readings locates new points within 0.25-0.53 mm at 1.5 N and over on a tip's own presses (normal force within 0.06-0.07 N on tips 0-2); on v2 ID 1 (five N52) a GP from the direction of the change, trained at 2 N and under, places 2-8 N presses within 0.25-0.31 mm and 5-6 % of the force (board GP 1.0-3.8 mm, 45-87 %); four N52 magnets (v3 ID 1) give half the signal per newton (28.3 against 52.3 uT/N) and the same calibrated errors (0.26 and 0.28 mm on the sphere, 0.36 and 0.33 mm on the rod, 1.21 and 1.10 mm on the tall indenter); a second four-magnet tip, v3 ID 2, matches v3 ID 1 on the presses both ran (28.2 against 28.8 uT/N; the five-magnet signal 1.83-1.87 times its own on the three indenters; 0.29 and 0.38 mm on the sphere, 0.36 and 0.36 mm on the rod), and its tip end is placed within 0.46 mm with the pass's other presses in training (2.98 mm from the grid alone); each indenter's presses, the tip end and slides are needed in a tip's training (an indenter left out: 0.57-1.80 mm against 0.25-1.05 mm with its own); on v3 IDs 1-3 the board GP's held-out location error falls from 0.56-0.63 to 0.46-0.51 mm from half to all of the training points; on v3 IDs 4-6 on the inverted rig it falls from 1.05-1.19 to 0.78-0.82 mm, with points 2.0 mm apart against 1.0 mm (0.32-0.37 mm against 0.27-0.30 mm on random holds with the load near the normal), and 66-71 new rod points per tip lower the error on the earlier points by 0.003-0.043 mm (0.54-0.73 mm among the new points), with a force angle of 3.0-4.7 deg against 2.8-3.1 deg with the load near the normal; v3 ID 3 gives 0.59 mm on the rig and 0.32 mm on the robot with the load near the normal, and its repeated presses vary by 7.9 % against 2.2-2.5 % in uT/N (stripped M2 holes in the seat block left the board loose, the most likely cause); pooled with IDs 4-6's rig holds, the GP of v3 IDs 1-3 reaches the pad's mount end (v3 ID 3's 70 holds there: 4.16 mm on its holds from the robot, 1.18 mm pooled; points on the robot 0.47-0.52 mm); the contact viewer's board GP was refitted with these holds on 11-05 (mount-end holds 3.04-3.10 to 0.75-0.77 mm, the robot's held-out points 0.38-0.46 to 0.45-0.53 mm); on v3 IDs 4-6 the other tips' holds lower the median held-out location error from 0.83 to 0.66 mm at new points and from 2.51 to 0.74 mm in a held-out pad region; an MLP ensemble on every hold gives 0.48-0.52 mm against the GP's 0.54-0.56 mm at held-out points and 1.00-1.03 against 1.24 mm in coverage gaps, where the GP's uncertainty ranks the errors better (Spearman 0.44 against 0.20-0.31); torsion not recovered (GP r 0.42, 0.38 and 0.21 on the twists; on v3 IDs 2 and 3 no better than predicting none); a GP trained on another tip gives 1.42 mm against 0.39 mm on the v1 tips and 1.02 and 1.30 mm against 0.51 and 0.38 mm between the four-magnet tips.

title: Calibration mount v5 with a PLA wedge behind the DIP link's tongue
page_title: Calibration mount v5 with a PLA wedge behind the DIP link's tongue
summary: Mount v5 = v4's fork as printed + a PLA wedge pushed into the stop plate's gap in place of three brass set screws: face-press turn to contact 1 -> 0.05 deg; the wedge closes gaps of 1.2-2.9 mm and locks by friction; >= 9.3 mm from the cell on the sphere and rod plans; two wedges in 14 min; not yet measured.

title: Calibration mount v4 with a stop behind the DIP link's tongue
page_title: Calibration mount v4 with a stop behind the DIP link's tongue
summary: Mount v4 = v3 + a stop plate behind the DIP link's tongue with three brass M3 set screws: the link's turn about the PIP axis under a face press falls from 1 to 0.05 deg; the plate stays 12 mm from the cell; fork reprint 1 h 46 min, 65 g; not yet printed or measured.

title: Transfer of the UR5 fingertip’s calibration to a second fingertip with two magnets reversed
page_title: Transfer of the UR5 fingertip’s calibration to a second fingertip with two magnets reversed
summary: The physical model rebuilt from the second fingertip's rest fit (two magnets reversed) placed six centre presses within 0.93 mm of their mean, 3.1 mm from the reference point, at 2.9 to 4.4 N. The UR5 fingertip's raw GP and MLP did not transfer (one answer for all presses; 9.9 mm), and its GP correction moved the points 2.3 mm toward the mount end. No force reference.

title: Rejection of fields from steel and other sources outside the pad in the fingertip’s contact estimator
page_title: Rejection of fields from steel and other sources outside the pad in the fingertip’s contact estimator
summary: Steel touched to the fingertip without force changed the reading by 217 to 360 uT and was estimated as 9.0 to 17.5 N presses. A test against a uniform field and a linear gradient across the board (threshold 25 in chi-square) cut the contact frames of six touches from 432 to 29 and rejected none of 737 UR5 holds. Toggle: key f, --foreign-gate.

title: Calibration of the lab's ATI Mini45 and Mini40 on the UR5 with a weighed mass
page_title: Calibration of the lab's ATI Mini45 and Mini40 on the UR5 with a weighed mass
summary: ATI Mini45 calibration with a weighed mass: coaxial stack from ATI drawing 9230-05-1094 (P1S, 3 h 28 min); 39 checked stations at five eyes, about 27 min; simulated sessions recover the sensor to 0.005 N and 0.4 N mm (medians) with 0.5 kg and to 0.021 N with the lab's 100 g weight in a printed holder; with the HEX-E as reference the error is up to 0.21 N, coaxial or turned 90 deg. The Mini40 gets its own base and top (ATI drawings 9230-05-1278, 9230-05-1314), 40 stations, and 0.0034 N with the 100 g weight in simulation.

title: Drift of the fingertip board's zero over a calibration session on the UR5
page_title: Drift of the fingertip board's zero over a calibration session on the UR5
summary: sphere2's board zero: 98 % of its 71 µT change is Earth's field, which the estimator absorbs; each press leaves a 7 µT step along its own change, 0.29 of it lasting and the rest fading in 19 s. Learned zeros lose to re-zeroing at rest, and the estimator's response (high at low force, 0.74 of the force at 3 to 5 N) dominates the error.

title: Pole pattern, registration and contact predictors of the first checkerboard fingertip on the UR5
page_title: Pole pattern, registration and contact predictors of the first checkerboard fingertip on the UR5
summary: On the first checkerboard fingertip (UR5 session cb1t, 2026-10-23), one pole pattern fits the field at rest, the planned checkerboard. Built from that fit alone, its physical model places held-out contacts within 2.06 mm (sphere2's tip 3.79 mm); sphere2's predictors miss by 2.5 to 8.6 mm, and 47 of its own presses give 0.42 to 0.71 mm.

title: Pad compliance, board response and contact predictors of the magnetic fingertip on the UR5
page_title: Pad compliance, board response and contact predictors of the magnetic fingertip on the UR5
summary: UR5 run sphere2: measured force is 0.20 of the FE pad's at the registered positions while the board reads 0.78-1.05 of the HEX-E's force; extra indentation 0.33 mm + 0.20 mm/N under the sphere, 0.07 mm + 0.10 mm/N under the rod; estimator 1.6-2.6 mm from 1 N; GP on 59 presses 0.84 mm, 0.09 N on held-out presses, 2.05 mm on rolls and twists; trained on all its presses, 0.80 mm on presses a day later.

title: Calibration protocol of the magnetic fingertip on the UR5 and the OptoForce HEX-E
page_title: Calibration protocol of the magnetic fingertip on the UR5 and the OptoForce HEX-E
summary: A protocol and program calibrate the magnetic fingertip on the lab's UR5 (CB3) and OptoForce HEX-E. The HEX-E is 35 mm tall, so the face centre is 128.4 mm from the flange. Homing on the indenter's key, a gravity sweep and 38 touch-offs measure the tool's pose; 74 presses and 19 slides, rolls and twists follow. In a simulated session the contact point on the pad is known within 0.07 mm (median) and the normal force within 0.4 %.

title: Fingertip calibration runs on the lab UR5 with the OptoForce HEX-E, 22 October 2026
page_title: Fingertip calibration runs on the lab UR5 with the OptoForce HEX-E, 22 October 2026
summary: First segment of the fingertip calibration on the lab UR5 (sphere2, 21:08 to 23:27): 29 touch-offs registered, 66 presses over the pad, 10 rolls and twists, reference presses steady within 0.07 mm; 4 flank presses carried a load off the pad. The HEX-E link's failures, the wrist's stop at the forearm and the twist on the homing key led to the program's checks.

title: UR5e calibration mount v3 with captive M6 × 20 screws
page_title: UR5e calibration mount v3 with captive M6 × 20 screws
summary: Mount v3 takes M6 x 20 screws: a 15 mm adapter sets 5.0 mm of thread in the HEX-E, the heads sit captive in the fork's foot and tighten from above, two with a straight key and two under the column with a ball-end key at 20 deg; everything above the foot rose 11 mm and the DIP links and indenters fit as in v2. Since 2026-10-22 the foot's four M3 go into brass heat-set inserts in 4.0 mm bores of the adapter.

title: Spherical and disc N52 magnets in the B00 fingertip pad
page_title: Spherical and disc N52 magnets in the B00 fingertip pad
summary: A 3 mm N52 sphere resolves 0.0285 N on pad B00 against 0.0304 N for the 3 x 2 mm disc of equal volume; spheres of 4 mm and more exceed the MLX90393's range at the five-magnet centres, and four 4 mm spheres on the four-magnet layout resolve 0.023 N if their walls pass.

title: HOM control of four demonstrated tasks across object sizes on the CAD-model SR2 hand
page_title: HOM control of four demonstrated tasks across object sizes on the CAD-model SR2 hand
summary: Under the HOM controller the pin-push held 11/12 rollouts (angle RMSE 2.5-4.4 deg on 16-40 mm cylinders), the press 7/12, rolling 12/12 and twisting 12/12. Pinned iCEM tracks the pinch angle to 0.5-0.6 deg against HOM's 2.5-3.0 deg in the pin-push and 8.7-11.2 deg in the press but squeezes with 14-22 N per pad against 4 N.

title: Hand-object mechanism control: the method and its MuJoCo implementation
page_title: Hand-object mechanism control: the method and its MuJoCo implementation
summary: The HOM paper's controller (GCFs, Eqs. 1-6, pinch and pusher) implemented as one MuJoCo library for position-servo hands, checked by 21 tests until they were removed on 2026-11-03; 15 differences from the paper listed, mostly servos for torque control and pads for hydroelastic contact; the three earlier controllers differ more.

title: DIP link b v4 and a sweep of retaining-wall heights
page_title: DIP link b v4 and a sweep of retaining-wall heights
summary: DIP link b v4 recesses the bridge's palmar edge to x_F -6.46 mm and shrinks the column under the pad, so a flat object meets the pad 4.0 mm before any rigid part (v3: 0.0 mm); the joint still stops on the horn arm at 93.0 deg. Covers I15 with 4, 3 and 2 mm walls and caps with 4, 3 and 2 mm blocks at 0.15 mm went to the owner's height test; the owner chose 3 mm, and the set of 2026-10-22 adds rails 0.10-0.16 mm tighter per flank and a 1.6 mm pin hole, which lock the pad in so tightly that it no longer sits flush; the owner kept that set for the retention on 2026-10-23, and the snug sets at zero interference are not used.

title: DIP link b v3 and UR5e calibration mount v2
page_title: DIP link b v3 and UR5e calibration mount v2
summary: Concept b becomes v3 and the UR5e mount v2 after the owner's first prints. The cover gains side walls along the pad's flanks, a column 0.6 mm inside the 11/22 outline replaces the neck, and the cable's leg opens to the top.

title: Model-based estimation of contact position and force on the magnetic fingertip
page_title: Model-based estimation of contact position and force on the magnetic fingertip
summary: A model of the five-chip board turns its 15 field components into a contact point and force anywhere on the pad's surface, from an FE basis at the 812 sphere pads; on simulated presses with N52 magnets the median errors are 0.18 mm and 0.03 N. In the first presses by hand the pad rocked in its seat, leaving offsets of 62-104 uT that read as standing contacts. The rest reading drifts 0.65-0.70 % of the field per degree C of chip temperature; a correction from each chip's temperature, a 2 uT noise floor and a re-zero after 3 s at rest stop the viewer showing contacts at rest.

title: Checks of the v2 11/22 fingertip and the 9.75 mm longer DIP link
page_title: Checks of the v2 11/22 fingertip and the 9.75 mm longer DIP link
summary: The calibration of 2026-10-18 applies to both v2 fingertips (a within 0.5 % RMS of the calibrated print, b 2.5 % stiffer). With the 11/22 tip b resolves 0.028 N against a's 0.065 N, as with the block.

title: Print sheet for the fit tests of DIP-link concept b, 19 October 2026
page_title: Print sheet for the fit tests of DIP-link concept b, 19 October 2026
summary: Two plates print the fit tests of DIP-link concept b, v2 (the link 9.75 mm longer, the Qwiic cable turned toward the back at the plug and routed past the slotted arm): 8 PLA pieces on the Bambu Lab P1S as one sliced Bambu Studio project (1 h 9 min, 18.3 g) and 5 Siraya Tech 85A groove blocks on one Bambu Lab P1S plate with the other run’s 85A blocks, from the external spool (26 min, 4.2 g for all 12).

title: Print sheet for the DIP-link fit tests of 19 October 2026
page_title: Print sheet for the DIP-link fit tests of 19 October 2026
summary: Two plates print every fit test of DIP-link concept a, v2 (the link 9.75 mm longer, with the Qwiic cable routed past the slotted arm): 12 PLA pieces on the Bambu Lab P1S as one sliced Bambu Studio project (2 h 10 min, 31.1 g) and 7 Siraya Tech 85A channel blocks on one Bambu Lab P1S plate with the other run’s 85A blocks, from the external spool (26 min, 4.2 g for all 12).

title: Calibration mount for the instrumented DIP link on a UR5e and HEX-E
page_title: Calibration mount for the instrumented DIP link on a UR5e and HEX-E
summary: Three PLA parts clamp a DIP link as printed (the CAD hand's, or v2 a or b of the DIP study, which keep its clevis arms within 0.01 mm) to the tool plate of an OnRobot HEX-E QC on the UR5e, so that the five magnetometers can be calibrated against the HEX-E.

title: Status of the printed-fingertip, contact-model and DIP-link work
page_title: Status of the printed-fingertip, contact-model and DIP-link work
summary: On 2026-10-18 the owner asked for nine things in one window: push everything, keep autopilot runs off the Max seat, a print procedure, a calibration of Drake's field and the pads to the finite elements (FE), the capsule and quarter-ellipsoid prints if they can be modelled, a DIP-link redesign that clamps the magnetometer board against the printed tip, and a file-explorer layout for the page index; at the printer the owner chose the 2.9 mm magnet seat.

title: Print procedure for the Siraya Tech 85A magnet fingertips on the Prusa XL
page_title: Print procedure for the Siraya Tech 85A magnet fingertips on the Prusa XL
summary: The 14 PrusaSlicer projects of the 85A set print the magnet fingertips in Siraya Tech TPU 85A on tool 2 of the Prusa XL, at 240 °C on a 35 °C bed. Print them in this order.

title: Calibration of Drake’s hydroelastic field and the 1 mm pads to finite elements of the printed 85A fingertips
page_title: Calibration of Drake’s hydroelastic field and the 1 mm pads to finite elements of the printed 85A fingertips
summary: None of the four printed 85A fingertips meets every criterion of the plan. One modulus fitted to the finite-element approach leaves the largest approach error at 41–61 % in Drake and gives the curved tips 1.2–1.7 times the print’s twist arm.

title: Magnetometer board mount in the DIP link for the printed 85A fingertips
page_title: Magnetometer board mount in the DIP link for the printed 85A fingertips
summary: The printable v2 of concepts a and b keeps the ReSkin 5X board's own Qwiic connector J1, as on the owner's board, and leads the Qwiic cable in a groove past the slotted arm to an anchor 5.0 mm below the PIP axis. Both DIP links are 9.75 mm longer, so the PIP axis lies 46.91 mm from the tip's end (37.16 mm today).

title: Deployment readiness of the CAD hand with printed 85A magnet fingertips
page_title: Deployment readiness of the CAD hand with printed 85A magnet fingertips
summary: Printed in Siraya Tech 85A at 30 % gyroid, the four-magnet fingertip block behaves on the hand’s tasks as the modelled TPU block did: the eight deployed bench plans keep the tool in 24 of 24 replays, within 1.9° RMS of Drake, and the four D6 policies hold it in 64 of 64 rollouts. Capsule and half-ellipsoid tips drop it.

title: Capsule and ellipsoid fingertips against the printed block on the SR2 hand
page_title: Capsule and ellipsoid fingertips against the printed block on the SR2 hand
summary: No curved fingertip beats the printed block on the SR2 hand’s tasks: of three finalists from nine shapes, the best, a 7.4 × 8.5 × 11/22 mm half-ellipsoid, changes the fresh-placement score by +0.053 (90 % interval -0.004 to +0.100). Curved tips cut the twist-onset arm to a third and the GPU step to 0.48–0.76 of the block’s, and the 16/32 mm half-ellipsoid follows Drake most closely along the bench replays.

title: Sphere-pad accuracy across fingertip geometry and fingertip co-design on the SR2 hand
page_title: Sphere-pad accuracy across fingertip geometry and fingertip co-design on the SR2 hand
summary: The 1 mm sphere pads reproduce the law’s twist-onset torque within 2 % on fillets of 1.5 mm or more and 7–14 % high on sharper edges, but their sliding torque grows with spin rate. At 1 rad/s the spin arm is 1.25 times the law on the printed tip’s 2.7 mm fillet and 1.73 times on a sharp block, while Drake stays within 0.97–1.12.

title: In-hand turn of cylinders on the scale-study layouts with the CAD-model hand under HOM control and sampling model-predictive control
page_title: In-hand turn of cylinders on the scale-study layouts with the CAD-model hand under HOM control and sampling model-predictive control
summary: The CAD-model hand, whose fingers reach 10.05 mm further than real_v1’s and collide through their printed links, has a feasible grasp in 39 cells of the scale study’s diagonal layouts with 10, 16 and 25 mm cylinders, against real_v1’s 34. HOM without the post turns the cylinder a median 30° per cell (real_v1 30°); with the post, the protocol of the bench plan, it reaches 60° in no cell.

title: Cost and control outcomes of the sphere-pad fingertip on the real_v1 hand
page_title: Cost and control outcomes of the sphere-pad fingertip on the real_v1 hand
summary: On the real_v1 hand the 1 mm sphere pads cost 147 µs per grip step on one CPU core (9.1 times point contact on the TPU block), 2.37 µs per MuJoCo-Warp world-step and 1.47 times the TPU mesh per PPO iteration. On the servo-limited plant they agree with Drake on 16 of 24 plan replays, against 1 for point contact, and their usable step is 2 ms.

title: Identification protocol for the SR2 hand’s serial-bus servos
page_title: Identification protocol for the SR2 hand’s serial-bus servos
summary: The servo plant behind every result since 2026-10-11 has an unmeasured strength: its 0.72 N m/rad gain is the load register’s slope scaled by a seller’s stall torque, and the replay fits could not tell gains of 0.25 and 8 apart. That gain decides whether the fingertip’s own deformation matters: with it the finger yields 3.4–4.7 mm/N, fifty times the printed gyroid tip.

title: In-hand turn of cylinders on the scale-study layouts under HOM control and sampling model-predictive control
page_title: In-hand turn of cylinders on the scale-study layouts under HOM control and sampling model-predictive control
summary: On the servo plant, HOM’s turn scores in the hand-object scale study record its governor and the support post more than the hand. In 17 of its 22 runs held at 60° or more, the cylinder swung on past the governor’s stop and came to rest on the post.

title: MLX90393 readout of printed fingertips on the five-chip board with one or four embedded magnets
page_title: MLX90393 readout of printed fingertips on the five-chip board with one or four embedded magnets
summary: eFlesh’s five-chip board reads one 141 Hz sample of the printed 20 % gyroid tip to 0.044 N with the Earth’s field removed, against 0.060 N from the chip under the magnet and 0.005 N on open eFlesh. The v17 finger’s 2.5 mm plate over the chips doubles it to 0.090 N.

title: Printability, stiffness and a one-command build of eFlesh lattice fingertips
page_title: Printability, stiffness and a one-command build of eFlesh lattice fingertips
summary: On the Prusa XL’s 0.4 mm nozzle, eFlesh’s lattice prints soundly at 8 mm cells and fails below: 3 %, 28 % and 71 % of each layer’s islands rest less than half on the layer below at 8, 6 and 4 mm cells. eFlesh’s cut-cell tool crashes on every input, so its notebook tiles whole cells and returns boxes; a one-command build now cuts the lattice to any closed shape, adds the magnet pouches and writes a PrusaSlicer project with the pause, in 9 s for the SR2 tip.

title: Sensitivity of the reorientation policies to fingertip contact parameters, with analytical checks of the sphere pads
page_title: Sensitivity of the reorientation policies to fingertip contact parameters, with analytical checks of the sphere pads
summary: On the servo-limited plant the reorientation policies need their feedback to cope with friction and servo strength, and hardly need it for the fingertip contact model. Replayed open loop on another tip model, a policy’s own actions hold the tool in 1,527 of 1,536 rollouts, against 1,531 closed loop, and end within 0.05 of the closed loop’s held cosine.

title: MuJoCo model of the SR2 finger assembled from its CAD parts, with sphere collision geometry
page_title: MuJoCo model of the SR2 finger assembled from its CAD parts, with sphere collision geometry
summary: A MuJoCo model of the SR2 finger, assembled from the STLs of its seven parts, keeps real_v1’s joint names, axes and mounts and its yaw-to-MCP (20.75 mm) and PIP-to-tip (37.16 mm) lengths. Its MCP link, the part mounted on the hand, spaces the MCP and PIP axes 30.80 mm apart against real_v1’s 20.75 mm, so the finger is 10.05 mm longer.

title: Presliding compliance from a sprung skin under the sphere pads
page_title: Presliding compliance from a sprung skin under the sphere pads
summary: The sprung skin mounts each pad’s spheres on a 2 g body held by springs at the fingertip’s elastic stiffness, so that a tangential load below slip deflects the contact and the deflection returns, as Mindlin’s solution gives for an elastic tip (40 µm at 1 N, 38 returned).

title: Reorientation policies with point-contact, pad and sprung-skin fingertips on the servo-limited plant
page_title: Reorientation policies with point-contact, pad and sprung-skin fingertips on the servo-limited plant
summary: The finger torque is limited to the SCS0009 servo’s 0.18 N m, and a penalty acts on fingertip force. The D6 policies with TPU-mesh and 1 mm pad fingertips then hold the screwdriver in 256 of 256 rollouts at 13–18 N (44–56 N at 1 N m).

title: Audit of the DiffMJX contact-gradient probes on the real_v1 D1 grasp
page_title: Audit of the DiffMJX contact-gradient probes on the real_v1 D1 grasp
summary: No policy was ever trained with DiffMJX; on 7 October the released fork’s derivatives were measured at the held D1 grasp over 1–20 ms, and 400 ms plans were searched in CPU MuJoCo.

title: Bench plan for the finger-spacing and object-size study
page_title: Bench plan for the finger-spacing and object-size study
summary: The bench week tests three predictions of a simulation whose finger servos have the SCS0009’s strength (0.72 N m/rad, 0.18 N m); the plan’s first version used a 1 N m plant.

title: Stiffness, sphere-pad calibration and embedded magnet of the printed TPU fingertip
page_title: Stiffness, sphere-pad calibration and embedded magnet of the printed TPU fingertip
summary: Finite-element models compare five whole-tip prints under the same screwdriver load (Table 1). Four have a 4.76 × 1.59 mm N52 magnet whose top lies 5 mm below the face.

title: Sphere-packed fingertip pads as a distributed contact model for dexterous manipulation in MuJoCo
page_title: Sphere-packed fingertip pads as a distributed contact model for dexterous manipulation in MuJoCo
summary: Covering a fingertip with small MuJoCo contact spheres samples the pressure law of hydroelastic contact, so unmodified MuJoCo reproduces the friction torque and contact area of a soft fingertip.

title: Finger-base spacing against object size on the SR2 hand
page_title: Finger-base spacing against object size on the SR2 hand
summary: Over 17 simulated layouts of the SR2 tripod and 18 objects, the layout with the largest fixed-contact workspace puts the mounts the object radius plus 35 mm (cylinders) or 37 mm (spheres) from its axis, about half the 68 mm finger. The task moves the optimum.

title: Sphere-packed fingertip pads as a distributed contact model for dexterous manipulation in MuJoCo
page_title: Sphere-packed fingertip pads as a distributed contact model for dexterous manipulation in MuJoCo
summary: Covering a fingertip with small MuJoCo contact spheres samples the pressure law of hydroelastic contact, so the pad reproduces the friction torque and contact area of a soft fingertip without modifying MuJoCo.

title: Performance, consistency and transfer of reorientation policies trained with four fingertip contact models
page_title: Performance, consistency and transfer of reorientation policies trained with four fingertip contact models
summary: Twelve PPO runs of up to 40 M steps in MuJoCo-Warp trained the D6 screwdriver turn. Replayed open loop in CPU MuJoCo, Drake and Newton, the finger targets of the pad and skin policies (1 mm sphere pads, bare or on a sprung skin) kept the tool in 216 of 220 replays.

title: Friction-row time constant, contact reduction and edge contact in Newton’s hydroelastic fingertip model
page_title: Friction-row time constant, contact reduction and edge contact in Newton’s hydroelastic fingertip model
summary: Newton’s friction-row time constant sets its creep and leaves its spin-onset torque unchanged. From 2 to 20 ms the twist creep rises tenfold while the onset arm stays within 2 %.

title: Presliding compliance, hysteresis and Hertz load exponents for sphere-pad fingertips with native MuJoCo elements
page_title: Presliding compliance, hysteresis and Hertz load exponents for sphere-pad fingertips with native MuJoCo elements
summary: The 1 mm sphere pads, point contact and Drake store no tangential displacement: under an axial force cycled at half the slip force they creep and recover nothing; Mindlin’s elastic contact moves 40 µm at 1 N and recovers 38. A spring-mounted skin under the pads gives 37 µm of recoverable presliding at 1.3× the pads’ GPU cost and keeps their pull, brake and twist results; the contact-model policies train on it.

title: Contact gradients for the real_v1 1 mm sphere-packed fingertip in native MJX and the released DiffMJX fork
page_title: Contact gradients for the real_v1 1 mm sphere-packed fingertip in native MJX and the released DiffMJX fork
summary: Native MJX 3.6 and the released fork completed one step of the 2,388-pad grasp with at most 1.84 µm initial tool-gap difference from CPU MuJoCo. Over 20 ms, the fork gradient selected a 0.1 rad control action that scored 0.111245 in CPU MuJoCo; CPU finite differences scored 0.111245 and the best of 128 samples scored 0.111241.

title: Sphere-packed fingertip pads as a distributed contact model for dexterous manipulation in MuJoCo
page_title: Sphere-packed fingertip pads as a distributed contact model for dexterous manipulation in MuJoCo
summary: Covering a fingertip with small MuJoCo contact spheres samples the pressure law of hydroelastic contact, so the pad reproduces the friction torque and contact area of a soft fingertip without modifying MuJoCo.

title: Contact release and reorientation after the real_v1 D1 grasp
page_title: Contact release and reorientation after the real_v1 D1 grasp
summary: In a 400 ms continuation of the D1 screwdriver grasp, numerical control derivatives improved the same sampled 1 mm packed-pad plan from 0.086 to 0.156 mean orientation gain with 8/8 perturbed grasps held. A sampled index release recontacted in 6/8 starts but gained 0.109 when held and failed on the convex mesh.

title: Servo plant refit, hand-object control of the three-finger turn, and the cost of sphere-pad fingertips in RL training
page_title: Servo plant refit, hand-object control of the three-finger turn, and the cost of sphere-pad fingertips in RL training
summary: Replaying 177 tracked bench runs fixes the simulated servo model. Fingers with a 0.02 s time constant and friction near 1 reproduce the joint readings within 2.89°, though the gain stays unidentified.

title: Friction creep, the printed TPU fingertip and the deployed three-finger reorientation in MuJoCo, MuJoCo-Warp and Drake
page_title: Friction creep, the printed TPU fingertip and the deployed three-finger reorientation in MuJoCo, MuJoCo-Warp and Drake
summary: MuJoCo’s friction creep falls as 1/impratio: under half the slip load the 1 mm sphere pads creep 0.31 µm/s at impratio 10 000 against 31 µm/s at 100 and 0.20 µm/s in Drake, while slip onset, twist onset and the brake change by at most 3 % and 1°. The printed TPU fingertip of the SR2 hand packed with 1 mm spheres matches Drake’s torsion onset within 5 %.

title: Sphere-packed fingertip pads as a distributed contact model for dexterous manipulation in MuJoCo
page_title: Sphere-packed fingertip pads as a distributed contact model for dexterous manipulation in MuJoCo
summary: Covering a fingertip with small MuJoCo contact spheres reproduces the friction torque and contact area of a soft pad without modifying MuJoCo. On the two-pad pinch of the real_v1 fingertip and screwdriver, the 1 mm pad slips at the same force as Drake hydroelastic to within 0.1 %, slides at a speed within 3 %, and starts to spin at a torque 6 % under Drake’s from 0.5 to 3 N.

title: Agreement and cost of five fingertip contact models on pinch, twist, roll, shake and brake tasks
page_title: Agreement and cost of five fingertip contact models on pinch, twist, roll, shake and brake tasks
summary: The 1 mm sphere pad spins the screwdriver at 6 % less torque than Drake hydroelastic from 0.5 to 3 N, slips at the same pull force, rolls the tool as Drake does and brakes the swing to within 1° of Drake. Its median deviation from Drake over nine metrics is 6.2 % in MuJoCo, 6.0 % in MuJoCo-Warp and 6.2 % in Newton, against 5.7 % for condim 4 and 95 % for point contact, which transmits no torque.

title: Contact models on robot tasks and sliding geometry
page_title: Contact models on robot tasks and sliding geometry
summary: On the SR2 pickup-to-insertion chain and a rolling-pinch task at 500 Hz control, the legacy MuJoCo sphere pads and Drake hydroelastic contact complete the chain, while 1 mm sphere pads with the physical-stiffness mapping tilt the tool during pickup and roll it weakly; 0.5 mm mapped spheres recover much of the rolling at higher CPU cost.

title: Specification of the distributed fingertip contact experiment
page_title: Specification of the distributed fingertip contact experiment
summary: This page reproduces the supplied DOCX specification unchanged, with its hypotheses and baseline claims. The measurements, which revise its static spring interpretation, are on the audit page.

title: Audit of the distributed sphere-pad fingertip contact in MuJoCo
page_title: Audit of the distributed sphere-pad fingertip contact in MuJoCo
summary: In MuJoCo the distributed sphere-pad fingertip reproduces the nominal screwdriver task, while its fixed contact mapping makes the force at a given indentation scale with the object’s mass, as the analytic stiffness prediction gives to floating-point precision.

title: Physics timestep sweep of the object-twist task at 50 Hz control
page_title: Physics timestep sweep of the object-twist task at 50 Hz control
summary: Over 42 cases of the object-twist task at 50 Hz control, seven contact variants at six physics steps from 0.05 to 10 ms with the same commands and gains, the legacy sphere pads and Drake complete the task at every step with tool roll gains of 0.57–0.63.

title: Native trajectories and close-ups of the fingertip contact models
page_title: Native trajectories and close-ups of the fingertip contact models
summary: Films of the force, holding, creep, payload, release and timestep runs of the distributed-contact audit, rendered from the saved states of each run: 1, 0.5 and 0.25 mm sphere pads in MuJoCo against Drake hydroelastic contact, the same pulse on CPU and GPU, and the cases that stopped at their guards.

title: Notes on grasp-force priors, Delassus coupling, TPU skin and a timestep benchmark
page_title: Notes on grasp-force priors, Delassus coupling, TPU skin and a timestep benchmark
summary: Research notes kept as a backlog: grasp-force priors predicted by a language and vision model (DeliGrasp), the Delassus operator as a tool for dense-contact coupling, a reduced model of the printed TPU skin, and a task-level timestep benchmark, which has since run (controller timestep page). The 2026-10-06 assessment of differentiable sphere pads is tabled at the end.

title: Articulated contact: holding, torsion and computational cost
page_title: Articulated contact: holding, torsion and computational cost
summary: With the same hand actuation in every backend, 1 and 0.5 mm sphere pads hold the screwdriver under 3 mN·m torque pulses and release it under 48 mN·m pulses, and keep 24.5 g and 196.3 g payloads and release 392.7 g. They creep inside the Coulomb bound, and a Cₜ/Cᵢ = 100 ramp starts sliding at 4.03 mN·m against Drake’s 4.66 on the same ramp.

title: Relative contact-velocity control of the screwdriver pick, braked swing, peg-hole insertion and wield on the SR2 hand in MuJoCo and Drake
page_title: Relative contact-velocity control of the screwdriver pick, braked swing, peg-hole insertion and wield on the SR2 hand in MuJoCo and Drake
summary: With the controller of Wang, Oh and Pollard, the SR2 hand picks the screwdriver, brakes its swing to hanging and inserts it in a peg hole, in simulation. The closed-loop brake ends the swing at 91.3° in Drake hydroelastic, 90.5° with 1 mm sphere pads and 88.2° with condim 4.

title: Pinch-brake loading of the screwdriver on the SR2 hand in Drake and MuJoCo
page_title: Pinch-brake loading of the screwdriver on the SR2 hand in Drake and MuJoCo
summary: On the SR2 hand (D8 gantry, calibrated position servos), thumb and index lower the real_v1 screwdriver from horizontal to hanging by relaxing their pinch, the load step of Wang, Oh and Pollard. Drake with hydroelastic fingertips at a 0.01 s relaxation passes 45° at 1.26 N and 80° at 0.40 N of pad force.

title: Pinch friction torque in Drake hydroelastic and MuJoCo contact models
page_title: Pinch friction torque in Drake hydroelastic and MuJoCo contact models
summary: On a two-pad rig gripping the screwdriver, Drake’s hydroelastic pad (E = 10 MPa) resists rotation about the pinch axis with μN·r̄ per pad, r̄ = 1.00 mm·(N / 1 N)0.25. MuJoCo matches this torque within 1 % with condim 4 and a torsional coefficient rescheduled from the normal force, and within 3–7 % with pads of 0.75 mm spheres.

title: Inverse kinematics and morphology–posture optimization of the SR² Hand in Drake
page_title: Inverse kinematics and morphology–posture optimization of the SR² Hand in Drake
summary: A Drake model built from the real_v1 MJCF matches MuJoCo’s fingertip poses and Jacobians to 2.78e-17 m over 128 configurations, and solves 7 of 7 inverse-kinematics problems (three mount layouts, frozen and with locked gantries, and one joint morphology–posture solve) within the joint limits, with at least 3.544 mm between enabled collision pairs, in about 1 ms each.

title: Grasp-to-gait chain with learned reorientation on the calibrated plant
page_title: Grasp-to-gait chain with learned reorientation on the calibrated plant
summary: Four learned reorientation policies on two hands, D5 and D6, run the whole chain on the calibrated plant (grasp, lift, learned turn, arm staging, seat, handover, gait) in 12 of 20 rollouts over five spawns, and every completed rollout turns the screw forward, 0.14–0.38 rev in eight gait cycles. The D1 and D2 policies lose the tool before the seat on every spawn.

title: Program record behind the SR2 Hand workshop paper
page_title: Program record behind the SR2 Hand workshop paper
summary: The workshop paper reports a sampling funnel, eight hands on a bench and a plan. Of 8,198 sampled finger layouts, 227 passed the simulated retention screen and its confirmation, 19 were exported as plans and eight were built.

title: Reorientation policies continued on the plant the chain and the bench use
page_title: Reorientation policies continued on the plant the chain and the bench use
summary: 10 of 12 continuation jobs trained (D4 stopped on NaN observations). Under ±3 mm / ±10° spawn jitter with friction DR the continued policies hold the tool in this many rollouts: D5 55, D5 + separation 55, D3 54, D3 + separation 51, D1 + separation 51, D6 48, D1 46, D6 + separation 45, D2 42, D7 28 of 64.

title: Reorientation policies across the deployed hands on the calibrated plant
page_title: Reorientation policies across the deployed hands on the calibrated plant
summary: Sixteen finetunes of one D6 policy train reorientation policies for the seven deployed hands, residual clipped at ±1 rad. Every hand has a policy holding the tool in 64 of 64 rollouts at the trained pose; those of D1, D3, D5 and D6 also turn it past cos 0.9 in every rollout.

title: D6 reorientation policy on the calibrated plant at 60 M steps, with a grip-force finetune
page_title: D6 reorientation policy on the calibrated plant at 60 M steps, with a grip-force finetune
summary: A finger-only policy on the calibrated plant turns the screwdriver from flat to cos 0.933 ± 0.003 (21° from vertical) and holds it on three pads in 64 of 64 deterministic rollouts. At 20 M steps the same recipe reads cos 0.463, and a second 60 M run stops at cos 0.641, a run-to-run band of at least 0.29.

title: Reorientation mechanism on the shipped, calibrated and bench plants
page_title: Reorientation mechanism on the shipped, calibrated and bench plants
summary: Every finger-driven reorientation the simulator has produced ran on a rigid, instantaneous actuator. On the actuator the bench calibrated, the fingers turn a gripped tool 1–8° on every hand at every setting tried.

title: Bench partial reorientation: support geometry, plan family and a two-tip gait
page_title: Bench partial reorientation: support geometry, plan family and a two-tip gait
summary: On the calibrated plant (kp 0.5) the deployed rv05 plan leaves the tool 50° from vertical (cos 0.638; bench 0.593), its upper end against the palm plate. The scene puts the plate on the mounting plane; on the built hand it is 25 mm higher, where the same plan tips the tool to 24, 34, 25° on the template contact model and drops it on the elliptic-cone model.

title: In-hand screwdriver reorientation on the calibrated plant by pinch and swing
page_title: In-hand screwdriver reorientation on the calibrated plant by pinch and swing
summary: On the bench-calibrated plant, the contact-fixed turn of every earlier result reaches only 0–20° from any grasp the fitter accepts. Releasing the middle finger instead lets the screwdriver swing tip-down about the thumb–index pinch under its own weight, ending at cos +0.92–0.98 on two pads.

title: Chain on the bench-calibrated plant
page_title: Chain on the bench-calibrated plant
summary: On the plant fitted to the bench on 2026-09-02 (finger gain kp 0.5, about 60× softer than the template’s), the chain’s 2 mm squeeze leaves 0–1.43 N of grip at the lift, and the plans’ own 10 mm lifts every hand at 2.5–4.5 N. The fingers then turn the tool only 0–10° at any travel budget, lagging their commands by 25–36°.

title: Basketball grasp on the real_v1 hand: reach, seating and held lift across three gantry layouts
page_title: Basketball grasp on the real_v1 hand: reach, seating and held lift across three gantry layouts
summary: A size-7 basketball is reachable on the real_v1 hand only as a friction cap grasp from above, at wrap angles up to 65° on the widest gantry layout, where it stops 18 mm short of the palm plate. Seating it needs a mount ring 5 mm wider than the gantries reach.

title: KaRMA rolling-pinch metric on the real_v1 design family
page_title: KaRMA rolling-pinch metric on the real_v1 design family
summary: KaRMA, a published kinematic score of thumb–index rolling-pinch dexterity, was computed for 504 real_v1 designs labelled by this program’s retention screen. It predicts which hands keep the screwdriver at AUC 0.802, +0.085 AUC above the best distance measurable off the mount plate, and ranks the residual clip a hand absorbs at ρ +0.363.

title: Screwdriver reorientation across eight deployed hands
page_title: Screwdriver reorientation across eight deployed hands
summary: In 2,214 simulated rollouts over 16 sweeps on the eight deployed hands, D6 completed the whole chain open loop on 3 of 4 seeds at one setting: pivot 0.15, travel budget 0.50 rad. The chain grasps the lying screwdriver, lifts it, turns it tip-down, seats it in a countersink and gaits it.

title: Training throughput on the workstation and a DeltaAI GH200
page_title: Training throughput on the workstation and a DeltaAI GH200
summary: A GH200 compute node runs the MuJoCo-Warp training loop at 0.74× the workstation’s median rate over its whole logged population (6,795 against 9,417 environment steps per second at 3,072 environments). Collection takes 98.7 % of each iteration and its cost per step is flat in batch width, so speed follows the GPU clock.

title: Screened plans in the chained task: pickup, turn and handover
page_title: Screened plans in the chained task: pickup, turn and handover
summary: The eight bench plans were rerun in simulation, alone and inside the chained task. Alone, the deploy screen reproduces the bench on the three best hands (held cosine 0.827, 0.726 and 0.568 against 0.834, 0.797 and 0.553).

title: Pad contact elevation and tool retention across eight deployed hands
page_title: Pad contact elevation and tool retention across eight deployed hands
summary: Retracted on 2026-09-06. The claimed rise from 18 to 30 full chains of 48 used a pad-target angle that counted a screwdriver standing on its handle as upright.

title: Effect of pivot height, residual clip and grasp fit on the deployed hands’ reorientation
page_title: Effect of pivot height, residual clip and grasp fit on the deployed hands’ reorientation
summary: Changing the one configuration that completes the chain (rv05_manual_stored, 169/169) toward the deployed plans one factor at a time identifies two causes of the lost reorientation.

title: Table-supported reorientation across sixteen hands
page_title: Table-supported reorientation across sixteen hands
summary: On a simulated UR5e, the table-supported maneuver stands the screwdriver upright in 177 of 256 runs across sixteen hands. Only 2 runs still hold it with two loaded pads at that moment, and in 116 stands no pad touches the tool.

title: Wrist geometry, payload declaration and grasp preload on the UR5e
page_title: Wrist geometry, payload declaration and grasp preload on the UR5e
summary: On a simulated UR5e told the hand’s mass, wrist stacks of 0 to 150 mm between flange and palm complete the grasp-to-gait chain in 8 of 8 seeds, and lowering the arm from a 300 mm pedestal to the table changes no result by more than one seed. Without the payload declared the wrist sags by up to 1.29 mm and a 150 mm stack completes 0 of 8.

title: Checks a sim-to-real residual must pass before the bench
page_title: Checks a sim-to-real residual must pass before the bench
summary: A residual reorientation policy for one hand can be built now: the corrected simulator plant matches rv05_manual on the bench (retention 0.94 against 0.92, held cosine 0.638 against 0.593), and the residual action term exists. A residual that controls many hands needs the design vector as an input, which is also unblocked.

title: Changing grasp without releasing the tool: relay hand-over and relay gait
page_title: Changing grasp without releasing the tool: relay hand-over and relay gait
summary: On rv05_manual_stored in simulation, a relay hand-over that moves one pad at a time onto the gait’s ring, followed by a gait that also releases one finger at a time, completes 6 of 6 seeds with 0.4 % of the task uncontacted, against 49 % when the hand opens and retakes the tool. It turns the tool 23.0° per cycle against 44.3°.

title: Carry-to-gait seam and countersink seating of the screwdriver
page_title: Carry-to-gait seam and countersink seating of the screwdriver
summary: In simulation one hand, rv05_manual_stored, completes the chain open loop (grasp, lift, stand upright, set down, release, re-index and gait) in 6 of 6 seeds on a floating palm and on a UR5e. The set-down is a race against a leaking grasp: the shaft creeps through the pads at about 1.5 mm/s, so each extra correction of the height costs grip (6 of 6 seeds for one move, 1 of 6 for eight).

title: Stiffness and overload cutoff of the SCS0009 finger servos
page_title: Stiffness and overload cutoff of the SCS0009 finger servos
summary: The SCS0009 finger servos behave as a position loop without an integral term: over 236 bench runs on 11 hands the joints stop short of their command by 0.0186° per unit of reported load, one constant for every loaded joint (R² 0.94–0.99), and a protective-torque cutoff at load 200 trips on 42 % of middle-yaw runs.

title: Open problems of the ground-supported gait
page_title: Open problems of the ground-supported gait
summary: After the ground-supported gait turned the standing shaft 4.99 revolutions in 40 cycles on rv05_manual, twelve follow-up studies were planned in three problems. The gait comes first: chain it to the carry, screen hands on release, load it, export it, close the loop; the chain and the load ran by 4 September.

title: Ground-supported gaiting
page_title: Ground-supported gaiting
summary: On rv05_manual, an open-loop cycle of twist, release, return and regrasp turns a screwdriver standing on the floor 4.99 revolutions about its axis in 40 cycles (SD 0.07, 3 rollouts), and the shaft ends 0.5° from vertical after 0.3 mm of drift. With the floor removed after the grasp, no hand keeps the shaft (0 of 6 rollouts each).

title: Tool pose from two AprilTags on the bench
page_title: Tool pose from two AprilTags on the bench
summary: Two AprilTags seen by the bench’s RealSense D435 measure the screwdriver’s tilt at 0.017° rms and its height at 0.030 mm rms, at 30 frames per second, where an operator had estimated the angle to about ±5°. Four tape measurements tie the camera to the simulator: a height on the bench equals the simulated height plus 44.0 mm.

title: Residual clip band, servo range and stall of the open-loop plans
page_title: Residual clip band, servo range and stall of the open-loop plans
summary: Every open-loop plan keeps the screwdriver only within a contiguous band of residual clips, and the 0.5 rad clip used in every screen so far came from Policy B’s action budget. Three plans on the bench ran below their band and drop the tool in every simulated repeat.

title: Reorientation across 108 real_v1 hand designs and the scores that predict it
page_title: Reorientation across 108 real_v1 hand designs and the scores that predict it
summary: Of 108 real_v1 hands sampled over the gantry workspace, each given a grasp sweep and a schedule sweep repeated under spawn jitter, 49 turn the shaft upright and keep it. Where the thumb pad sits along the shaft decides it: sliding the thumb 20 mm takes rv04_mid from 0 of 8 to 8 of 8, and the thumb’s moment arm about the pinch axis separates turning from non-turning designs at AUC 0.821.

title: Residual RL on a scheduled anchor and an open-loop carry to vertical
page_title: Residual RL on a scheduled anchor and an open-loop carry to vertical
summary: On the real_v1 hand modelled from its CAD, a residual PPO policy riding a scheduled second grasp anchor turns the screwdriver to cos +0.848 ± 0.003 on rv05_manual and holds it in 3 of 3 rollouts; the same recipe without the anchor ends at −0.014.

title: Rotational lock in the fixed-contact turn
page_title: Rotational lock in the fixed-contact turn
summary: Four real_v1 designs, with mounts up to 60 mm apart, held the screwdriver through the hand-off from Policy A to Policy B and turned it by 0.9–4.0°. The fitted grasp caused this: each finger had 1.3–7.1 mm of extension left on its 68.11 mm chain, and a turn about the pinch axis costs extension, which caps the turn at 2.5–10.2° in the order training found.

title: Grasp, lift and hand-off of the real_v1 hand built from the CAD, in simulation
page_title: Grasp, lift and hand-off of the real_v1 hand built from the CAD, in simulation
summary: After three fixes to the model, the real_v1 hand built from its CAD grasps and lifts the screwdriver in simulation, provided the pads close on the shaft’s equator: 10.1° above it, the grip force decayed from 1.75 N to zero within 0.6 s of holding, and softer pads or higher friction did not change that.

title: Screwdriver reorientation: two finger arrangements compared
page_title: Screwdriver reorientation: two finger arrangements compared
summary: In simulation, the opposed pair of fingers (policy r4) turns a screwdriver from flat to vertical in 64 of 64 rollouts, to cos 0.995, and drops it in every one at step 389 ± 25: the shaft turns by sliding 44.8 mm through a two-point pinch, so the turn uses up the pad. The inline pair opposing the thumb (policies a10→b33) turns it to cos 0.911 and holds it with three loaded fingers.
